apps.localizedDescription:
Gallery. Studio. Film Lab.

your photos. your workflow. your app.

Make a look in a click or take control of every detail. Chromasmith is a free photo studio with 133 calibrated film looks, real grain, halation and bloom, RAW development, masks and retouching, a local photo library and full-resolution export — running entirely on your own device. No account, no upload, no subscription. The web version is a single HTML file with no build step and no server behind it.

A gallery for every shoot:

Faces, pets, favourites and keywords are found for you, on your own machine. Click a photo to preview it, or try a filter.

A studio for every frame:

Six tools, one editor: pick a look, shape the light and colour, add texture, then crop and frame for output.

versions.localizedDescription:
macOS:

• Drag Chromasmith into your Applications folder.
• Right-click the app and choose Open, then Open again.

macOS asks that once because the app is not signed with a paid Apple developer certificate. After the first launch it opens normally.

Intel build. On an Apple Silicon Mac it runs under Rosetta 2 — macOS offers to install that automatically the first time. This is because the bundled ONNX Runtime has no Apple Silicon build at the pinned version.

Windows:

• Windows SmartScreen will warn the app is from an "unknown publisher" — click More info, then Run anyway. This is because the installer is not code-signed (no paid certificate). It's the same trust gap as macOS's Gatekeeper warning above, just a different OS's version of "the author isn't a company Microsoft/Apple has vetted.".
• The installer registers Chromasmith as a handler for TIFF/JPEG/PNG/RW2 files and for Adobe's OAuth sign-in redirect, so double-clicking a photo or signing in to Adobe from within the app both work immediately.

Bundled on-device AI models keep their own licences, two of which are non-commercial/research — see.
